topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Understand that living things grow, take in nutrients, breathe, reproduce eliminate waste and die.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Discuss that living things need energy to grow, live and be healthy, and plants get their energy from light (photosynthesis) while animals get their energy from eating plants and other animals.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Explore the requirements of plants for life and growth (air, light, water, nutrients from soil, and room to grow).

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Recognize cells as the basic unit of life that are organized into tissues, organs, systems and organisms.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Arrange and rank different levels of cellular organizations — cells to tissues, organs and organisms.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Relate the structures of some common cells (nerve, muscle, epithelium and blood cells) to their functions.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Describe variation and adaptation in living organisms.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Explain and illustrate the differences between variation and adaptation.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Identify sources of variation from environmental and genetic factors.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Explain how different adaptations affects the chances of survivals of different species of organism.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Identify the structures present in an animal cell and plant cell as seen under a simple microscope and relate them to their functions (only cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, cell wall, chloroplast, mitochondria and sap vacuole).

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Describe the similarities and differences between the structures of plant and animal cells. Sketch the animal and plant cells and label key organelles in each.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Compare and contrast an animal cell and plant cell by preparing slides using onion peels and cheek cells.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Recognize Genetics as the study of Heredity and understand and define heredity as the transfer of genetic information that specifies structure, characteristics, and functions, from parents to offspring.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Differentiate between the concept of genes and chromosomes and relate them to how genetic characteristics are inherited.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Describe the composition and structure of DNA.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Design a model of DNA to demonstrate its structure, functions, and various components.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Describe cell division and its types — mitosis and meiosis and relate them to the passage of genetic information through reproduction.

topic: 1. Organisms - Characteristics and Life Processes of Living Things
outcome: Explain the process of mitosis and meiosis and identify their key phases.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Classify the plants into two major groups (flowering, non- flowering), and give examples of each group.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Describe the functions of different parts of flowering plants: Roots, stem/ trunk, leaves and flowers.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Describe the different types of reproduction of plants.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Compare and contrast types of reproduction (sexual and asexual) in plants.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Distinguish between artificial and natural asexual reproduction in plants. (Budding, grafting, Bulbs, Tuber, Runners, cutting, and layering.)

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Inquire how artificial propagation can lead to better quality yield in agriculture.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Investigate the way in which water is transported within plants.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Identify the parts of the plant transport system and describe their functions (stem, -leaf, -root). Note: - Recall of the relative positions of water and food carrying tubes is not required. - The use of specific terms (‘xylem’ and ‘phloem’) is not required.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Identify the parts of a flower and describe their functions (limited to petals, sepals, anthers, filaments, stamens, stigma, style, carpel, and ovary).

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Explain the root and shoot system in plants. Label different parts of leaf, stem and root (external and internal structure).

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Predict the role of xylem and phloem in transport of water and food in plants by observing the cross section of the stem.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Define the process of photosynthesis and derive word equations for it.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Explore the role of flowers in the life cycle of flowering plants, including pollination, fruit and seed formation and seed dispersal.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Describe seed germination and know that seeds require water and an appropriate temperature to germinate.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Identify stages in the life cycles of common flowering plants.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Relate that why plants are vital to sustaining life on Earth.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Identify various professions associated with this unit of science. E.g., botanists, farmers, gardeners, florists, etc.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Know that plants require minerals to maintain healthy growth and life processes (limited to magnesium to make chlorophyll and nitrates to make protein).

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Explain that the structure of leaves is adapted to the process of photosynthesis.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Describe the process of respiration and write word equations for it. Compare and contrast the processes of photosynthesis and respiration.

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Investigate the phenomena of transpiration and its importance in a plant (wind, temperature, light, humidity affecting rate of transpiration in plants).

topic: 2. Organisms - Structure and Functions (Plants) - How plants use their body structures to survive?
outcome: Explore and apply natural raise of water based on the principle of transpiration.

Distinguish between major groups of animals with backbones (vertebrates: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals) and without backbones (invertebrates: Insects, snails, earthworm, jellyfish and corals) on the basis of their characteristics.

Identify that the human body has a number of systems, each with its own function.

Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
Trace the path of air in and out of the body and how the oxygen it contains is used during the process of respiration.

Describe the role and function of major organs in the human respiratory system including trachea, lungs and alveoli (air sacs).

State the importance of digestion in the human body and describe physical and chemical digestion.
Sequence the main regions of Alimentary Canal, its associated organs and describe the functions of different parts of the Alimentary Canal.
Briefly describe the role of enzymes in digestion.
Describe the structure and function of the human heart.
Explain how blood circulates in the human body through a network of vessels (arteries, veins and capillaries), and transports gases, nutrients, wastes and heat.
Compare and contrast arteries, veins and capillaries.
Describe the composition of blood and the functions of red cells, white cells, platelets and plasma.
Recognize that humans have different types of teeth (molar, premolar, incisors, canine) and know their functions in digestion of food.
Investigate the causes and prevention of tooth decay and gum diseases.
Identify by name the main parts of the Human Circulatory System, and describe briefly the functions of the heart, blood vessels and blood.
Describe the structure of the cerebrum, its division into two hemispheres (left and right) and the role of each hemisphere in the control of the body.
Identify that many vertebrates have a digestive system similar to humans.
Identify that many animals have a circulatory system similar to humans.
Conclude that blood transports the products of digestion to other parts of the body and the undigested products get egested/defecated.
Explain and represent how messages flow through the body from and to the brain, and how the brain collaborates with the sensory organs to regulate this process.
Map the various steps in the transmission of messages through the body and to the brain.
Describe the role and function of neurons in transmitting messages through the body.
Predict what would happen if a nerve connection broke.
Match various body functions with the relevant part of the brain that controls or regulates them (for instance, associating breathing with the brain stem).
Recognize the items of the first aid box.
Use a first aid box to dress a wound.

Identify the constituents of a balanced diet for humans as including protein, carbohydrates, fats and oils, water, minerals (limited to calcium and iron) and vitamins (limited to A, C and D), and describe the functions of these nutrients.
Identify the essential nutrients, their chemical composition, and food sources.
Identify and describe essential nutrients’ deficiency disorders.
Recognize that a healthy diet contains a balance of foodstuffs.
Correlate diet and fitness.
Define and describe main groups of microorganisms (bacteria, virus and fungi) and give examples of each.
Recognize some common diseases of each group (bacteria, virus and fungi) caused by microorganisms.

outcome: Describe the role of living things in cycling oxygen and carbon through an ecosystem, citing the processes of respiration, photosynthesis, and combustion.

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
outcome: Relate how oxygen and carbon cycles are complementary processes that bring balance and symmetry to life on Earth.

outcome: Describe global warming and explain how threats to the carbon-oxygen balance such as overpopulation, reliance on fossil fuels, and deforestation are contributing to global warming and climate change.

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
outcome: Describe how energy flows from producers to consumers, and how only part of the energy flows from one level of the pyramid to the next.

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
outcome: Predict how changes in an ecosystem (e.g., changes in the water supply, the introduction of a new population, hunting, migration) can affect available resources, and thus the balance among populations.

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
outcome: Describe how plants and animals adapt to environments that are hot, cold, wet and/or dry and describe common physical adaptations of plants (e.g., a thick stem, a waxy coating helps it survive with less water) and animals e.g., colours of animals help in camouflage.

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
outcome: Associate behaviors of animals with the environments in which they live, and describe how these behaviors help them to survive (e.g., migration and hibernation).

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
outcome: Explain ways in which human behavior (e.g., replanting forests, reducing air and water pollution, protecting endangered species) can have positive effects on the local environment.

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
outcome: Explore how human actions such as urbanization and population growth can affect a habitat.

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence

topic: 5. Ecosystems - Conditions for life on Earth/ Biodiversity and Interdependence
